tool.name: lighter
tool.description: kmer-based error correction for WGS reads
tool.command: ## Lighter derives the name of each corrected file from the input basename ## ('X.fq' -> 'X.cor.fq'), so stage every input under a predictable name first. ## ## The staged names always end in '.gz': Lighter only gzip compresses its output ## when the read file name ends in 'gz' and the compression level is > 0, and its ## gzip reader transparently accepts uncompressed data. Staging every input under a ## '.gz' name therefore makes the output gzip compressed regardless of whether the ## incoming dataset was compressed or not. #set $counter = 0 #for $file in $r: ln -s -f '${file}' input_${counter}.fastq.gz && #set $counter = $counter + 1 #end for lighter #set $counter = 0 #for $file in $r: -r input_${counter}.fastq.gz #set $counter = $counter + 1 #end for #if str($kmer.k_select) == "smallk": -k $kmer.k_parameter_string #elif str($kmer.k_select) == "bigK": -K $kmer.K_parameter_string #end if -od ./ -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4}" ## Compression level of the corrected reads. The level only takes effect because ## the staged input names end in '.gz' (see above). -zlib 1 #if str($maxcor): -maxcor $maxcor #end if $trim $discard $noQual #if str($newQual): -newQual '$newQual' #end if $stable && ## Lighter writes one corrected file per input into the output directory; concatenate ## them into the single Galaxy output dataset. Concatenating gzip members yields a ## valid gzip stream, so the members can simply be cat'ed together. The stem is ## globbed because Lighter picks '.cor.fa' or '.cor.fq' from the file content, not ## from the file name. cat /dev/null > $outfile #set $counter = 0 #for $file in $r: && cat input_${counter}.cor.* >> $outfile #set $counter = $counter + 1 #end for

param.name: k_select
param.label: Kmer mode
param.option: -k: supply kmer length, genome size and alpha
-K: supply kmer length and genome size, Lighter estimates alpha

param.name: k_parameter_string
param.label: kmer_length genome_size alpha
param.help: Three space separated values: kmer length, genome size and the sampling rate alpha. A good starting point for alpha is 7 / coverage.

param.name: K_parameter_string
param.label: kmer_length genome_size
param.help: Two space separated values: kmer length and genome size. Lighter estimates alpha from the average coverage in an extra pass over the reads.

param.label: Maximum number of corrections allowed per read
param.help: Setting this value explicitly disables Lighter's automatic adjustment of the value when the error rate is high.

param.label: Allow trimming of reads with low quality stretches
Discard reads that cannot be corrected
param.help: Discarded reads are not written to the output, which breaks the matching of paired end reads.

param.label: Ignore the quality scores of the input reads
Quality string used for corrected bases
param.help: Only the first character is used, e.g. 'I' for a quality of 40.

param.label: Keep the output stable across runs

tool.help:
**What it does**
**Lighter** is a kmer-based error correction method for whole genome sequencing data. Lighter uses sampling (rather than counting) to obtain a set of kmers that are likely from the genome, and uses that information to correct reads containing sequence errors.
Because no kmer counting is performed, Lighter is fast and needs little memory, which makes it suitable for large whole-genome sequencing datasets.
-----
**Choosing -k or -K**
* `-k kmer_length genome_size alpha` -- you supply the sampling rate `alpha` yourself. A good starting point is `alpha = 7 / coverage`. * `-K kmer_length genome_size` -- Lighter estimates `alpha` from the average coverage in an extra pass over the reads, which requires a reasonably accurate `genome_size`.
The `genome_size` should be at least the size of the sequenced genome.
-----
**Output**
The corrected reads of all input files are returned in a single gzip compressed dataset. Lighter annotates each read header with its correction status, for example `cor` (corrected), `bad_suffix` / `bad_prefix` (low quality stretch) or `unfixable_error`, with the reason being `lc` (low coverage), `ak` (ambiguous candidate kmer) or `oc` (over-corrected).
-----
**Notes**
* `-stable` is accepted for backwards compatibility but is a no-op in current Lighter releases; the corrected output is already reproducible across runs and thread counts. * Lighter 1.1.2 added `-saveTrustedKmers` / `-loadTrustedKmers` for persisting the trusted kmer set between runs. `-saveTrustedKmers` makes Lighter stop after the sampling stage without writing any corrected reads, so these options are not exposed here.
